q: What is a single point of failure?
a: A component whose failure alone takes down the whole system — for example, one web server with no peer.

q: Why do replicas need a load balancer in front of them?
a: Copies alone do not reroute traffic; the balancer spreads requests across healthy backends and skips the dead one.

q: What did the kill-node chaos prove in this lab?
a: The single server failed every request, while the replicated pair kept passing — redundancy plus routing removes the SPOF.
